items.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019
items.q: Eastman, that’s not what they do.

ctx.x: Well people have to find their own way to some extent anyway. I just sometimes worry about — I might have had the next you know really big player under my tutelage and I sort of took them on the broad path instead of the narrow path. Of course normally if I get a really, really good student, I tell them they need to go to somebody else if they get to a point where I can’t help you anymore.

Well yeah, we all should do it. It happens to me too, it’s great. Since we’re talking about education I’m going to a conservatory and it’s a bunch of race horse types, all trying to win you know, they really are taking it — involved with music and be, whatever. The skill will be moving all those great demands and be a fine musician. And most of the rewards, courses that I took as an undergraduate, were adequate to say the least. I mean there were a couple of wonderful professors that I had, but Eastman, that’s…
You have a 30-year-old daughter you said?
